story:
In a certain hillside orchard, the gardener follows one unbreakable habit. Take any two cuttings at all — call the first quince and the second medlar.

She grafts medlar onto quince and sets the result aside as Graft 1.

However she chooses her two starting cuttings, quince itself and Graft 1 always grow into exactly the same plant. That is simply how this orchard works, without exception.

One spring her neighbor wonders about something. Take any two cuttings — again call the first quince and the second medlar. Graft quince onto medlar and set the result aside as Graft 1.

In this orchard, must quince itself and Graft 1 always grow into the same plant?

GIVEN: x = f(y, x)
SHOW: x = f(x, y)
label: RG-2

story:

He feeds hum through whistle and sets the result aside as Relay 1; then he feeds Relay 1 through hum and calls the result Relay 2; then he feeds Relay 2 through whistle and calls that Relay 3.

However he chooses his two starting signals, whistle itself and Relay 3 always sound exactly alike. That is simply how this station works, without exception.

One night his trainee wonders about something. Take any two signals — again call the first whistle and the second hum. Feed whistle through hum and set the result aside as Relay 1.

At this station, must whistle itself and Relay 1 always sound exactly alike?

SHOW: x = f(x, y)
label: RG-2

He feeds hum through hum and sets the result aside as Relay 1.

However he chooses his two starting signals, whistle itself and Relay 1 always sound exactly alike. That is simply how this station works, without exception.

One night his trainee wonders about something. Take any two signals — again call the first whistle and the second hum. Feed whistle through hum and set the result aside as Relay 1; then feed hum through hum and call the result Relay 2; then feed Relay 1 through Relay 2 and call that Relay 3.

At this station, must whistle itself and Relay 3 always sound exactly alike?

She pours ochre into crimson and sets the result aside as Batch 1; then she pours crimson into ochre and calls the result Batch 2; then she pours Batch 1 into Batch 2 and calls that Batch 3.

However she chooses her two starting pigments, crimson itself and Batch 3 always come out the exact same color. That is simply how this workshop works, without exception.

One morning her apprentice wonders about something. Take any two pigments — again call the first crimson and the second ochre. Pour crimson into ochre and set the result aside as Batch 1.

In this workshop, must crimson itself and Batch 1 always come out the same color?
completion:
GIVEN: x = f(f(y, x), f(x, y))
SHOW: x = f(x, y)
label: RG-2

She grafts damson onto medlar and sets the result aside as Graft 1; then she grafts Graft 1 onto damson and calls the result Graft 2; then she grafts medlar onto Graft 2 and calls that Graft 3.

However she chooses her three starting cuttings, quince itself and Graft 3 always grow into exactly the same plant. That is simply how this orchard works, without exception.

One spring her neighbor wonders about something. Take any two cuttings — again call the first quince and the second medlar. Graft medlar onto quince and set the result aside as Graft 1.

In this orchard, must quince itself and Graft 1 always grow into the same plant?

In the first, she grafts quince onto medlar and sets the result aside as Graft 1.

However she chooses her four starting cuttings, Graft 1 and Graft 3 always grow into exactly the same plant. That is simply how this orchard works, without exception.

One spring her neighbor wonders about something. Take any two cuttings — again call the first quince and the second medlar. Graft medlar onto quince and set the result aside as Graft 1.

In this orchard, must quince itself and Graft 1 always grow into the same plant?

He feeds chirp through buzz and sets the result aside as Relay 1; then he feeds whistle through Relay 1 and calls the result Relay 2; then he feeds hum through Relay 2 and calls that Relay 3.

However he chooses his four starting signals, whistle itself and Relay 3 always sound exactly alike. That is simply how this station works, without exception.

One night his trainee wonders about something. Take any two signals — again call the first whistle and the second hum. Feed hum through hum and set the result aside as Relay 1.

At this station, must whistle itself and Relay 1 always sound exactly alike?

She pours ochre into teal and sets the result aside as Batch 1; then she pours Batch 1 into indigo and calls the result Batch 2; then she pours crimson into Batch 2 and calls that Batch 3; then she pours Batch 3 into ochre and sets the result aside as Batch 4.

However she chooses her four starting pigments, crimson itself and Batch 4 always come out the exact same color. That is simply how this workshop works, without exception.

One morning her apprentice wonders about something. Take any two pigments — again call the first crimson and the second ochre. Pour ochre into ochre and set the result aside as Batch 1.

In this workshop, must crimson itself and Batch 1 always come out the same color?

She grafts medlar onto medlar and sets the result aside as Graft 1; then she grafts quince onto Graft 1 and calls the result Graft 2.

Graft damson onto damson and set the result aside as Graft 1; then graft medlar onto Graft 1 and call the result Graft 2; then graft Graft 2 onto medlar and call that Graft 3.

In this orchard, must quince itself and Graft 3 always grow into the same plant?

In the first, she grafts quince onto quince and sets the result aside as Graft 1.

In the second, she grafts medlar onto medlar and calls the result Graft 2.

However she chooses her two starting cuttings, Graft 1 and Graft 2 always grow into exactly the same plant. That is simply how this orchard works, without exception.

One spring her neighbor wonders about something. Take any two cuttings — again call the first quince and the second medlar. Graft quince onto quince and set the result aside as Graft 1. Separately, graft medlar onto quince and call the result Graft 2; then graft Graft 2 onto quince and call that Graft 3; then graft medlar onto Graft 3 and set the result aside as Graft 4.

In this orchard, must Graft 1 and Graft 4 always grow into the same plant?

She grafts quince onto medlar and sets the result aside as Graft 1; then she grafts Graft 1 onto damson and calls the result Graft 2; then she grafts Graft 2 onto damson and calls that Graft 3.

However she chooses her three starting cuttings, quince itself and Graft 3 always grow into exactly the same plant. That is simply how this orchard works, without exception.

One spring her neighbor wonders about something. Take any four cuttings — again call the first quince, the second medlar, the third damson, and the fourth mulberry. Graft medlar onto damson and set the result aside as Graft 1; then graft Graft 1 onto mulberry and call the result Graft 2; then graft Graft 2 onto medlar and call that Graft 3.

In this orchard, must quince itself and Graft 3 always grow into the same plant?

In the first, he feeds whistle through hum and sets the result aside as Relay 1; then he feeds whistle through Relay 1 and calls the result Relay 2; then he feeds Relay 2 through hum and calls that Relay 3.

In the second, he feeds chirp through chirp and sets the result aside as Relay 4; then he feeds whistle through Relay 4 and calls the result Relay 5; then he feeds whistle through buzz and calls that Relay 6; then he feeds Relay 5 through Relay 6 and sets the result aside as Relay 7.

However he chooses his four starting signals, Relay 3 and Relay 7 always sound exactly alike. That is simply how this station works, without exception.

One night his trainee wonders about something. Take any two signals — again call the first whistle and the second hum. Feed whistle through hum and set the result aside as Relay 1; then feed Relay 1 through hum and call the result Relay 2. Separately, feed hum through hum and call that Relay 3; then feed Relay 3 through whistle and set the result aside as Relay 4; then feed Relay 4 through hum and call the result Relay 5.

At this station, must Relay 2 and Relay 5 always sound exactly alike?
